subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose broad private-network access for arbitrary `web_fetch` URLs, and if so should it be global, per-agent, hostname-scoped, or kept behind a narrower policy surface?
rationale: This changes an SSRF boundary and public config contract; current source and v2026.6.11 do not expose the requested key, and a maintainer comment explicitly leaves the metadata/LAN/redirect policy unresolved.

options.title: Approve scoped SSRF policy
options.body: Land a dangerous, explicit `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy` design with audit, cache, redirect, metadata/link-local, and per-agent authorization semantics.

options.title: Keep only narrow fake-IP support
options.body: Leave current main as-is and document that arbitrary private-network `web_fetch` remains intentionally unsupported for now.

options.title: Fold into egress firewall work
options.body: Make this part of the broader web-tool egress firewall design so private-network access and domain allowlists share one policy model.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped SSRF policy
recommendation.body: Land a dangerous, explicit `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy` design with audit, cache, redirect, metadata/link-local, and per-agent authorization semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: They made the clearest maintainer-side security-boundary comment on this issue and are tied to recent SSRF/guarded-fetch work.
